newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- The State Commission for Restructuring the Economy lists number of major reforms of economic structure this year, with reform of state-owned enterprises as top priority.

- Film makers should produce more and better films that depict socialist cultural and ethical progress, says Politburo member Ding Guangen. Films should make more economic returns while attaching importance to social effect
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- Chinese Government is ready to work with the Bolivian Government to develop long-term, stable and all-round friendship and cooperative ties through 21st century, President Jiang Zemin tells visiting Bolivian President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada.
CHINA SECURITIES
- China Securities Regulatory Commission to punish listed firms that provide false information in annual reports
- China issues detailed rules on adjustment of taxeson banks and insurers
- China seen unlikely to cut interest rates in first half
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Combined assets of foreign financial institutions in Shanghai reach $5.3 billion at end-1996, outstanding loans at $3.7 billion
- China Everbright Bank opens branch in Guangzhou
- China Merchant Bank opens branch in Hangzhou
ECONOMIC DAILY
- State Land Administration issues tern warning that farm land being eroded by urban expansion and bline land use
- Central bank survey finds current bank deposits increase in 1996 while fixed deposits decline
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- Official of Civil Aviation General Administration says five of China's 27 airlines reported losses in 1996
- Air China made profits of 10 billion yuan in 1996, foreign competition seen posing threat to China's airlines
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- China demand for integrated circuits seen at 4.0 billion in 1997
CHINA DAILY
- Foreign Ministry condemns meeting between Dalai Lama and so-called Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui
- China campaign to relieve poverty, promote education and technology and improve health of people in rural areas will receive aid from United Nations Development Programme
